content.comment_body: Hello, Could you share how you resolved the problem? I'm experiencing something similar. My network project includes three [product_name], one [product_name] (previous version), and an operator panel ([product_name]). One of the [product_name] units switches from RUN to STOP mode daily, and I have to connect a PC to the network to restore RUN mode.

There is a discussion about this issue in the German-speaking section of the forum. It seems to affect the [product_name] with [article_no] and certain firmware versions. According to feedback, older versions do not show the error. [company_name] has been informed and is reportedly investigating, but no solution has been communicated yet. You should also consider submitting a support request.
What firmware version does your [product_name] use?
Consider creating a support request and contacting [company_name] directly. See this related topic in German: [url]

Although this topic is older and the specific models are no longer sold, I recently completed a home automation setup using three [product_name] units and several extension modules. Two were purchased used and both run firmware [version_no]. I'm also encountering the STOP issue, which seems related to using network inputs and outputs. Does the problem arise only with network inputs, outputs, or both? I can adjust my setup to reduce network links if I know which situations trigger STOP mode. Any insights are appreciated.
The issue appears when [product_name] devices are networked (for example, connected to another [product_name], a PLC, operator panel, or similar equipment).

Thank you for confirming. I plan to switch to spare Digital IO instead of sending Boolean signals over the network. For analogue values, I'll reconfigure wiring to keep all analogue IO with its own extension module. This should allow me to avoid network communication, except for program uploads or debugging via [product_name] software.
Yes, that's a good approach. If the [product_name] units are used as standalone devices and not networked, the error should not happen.

analysis.insight_summary: Users have noticed that [product_name] units, especially those with firmware [version_no], may randomly switch from RUN to STOP mode when connected in a network with other automation devices. This problem occurs roughly daily and particularly affects devices involved in network communication, while standalone units are unaffected. Manual intervention is needed to restore normal operation, causing inconvenience.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect stable and uninterrupted operation from the [product_name] when used in networked environments. They seek clear information about the cause of the STOP mode issue and a practical solution, hoping to avoid frequent manual resets and gain confidence in the networked system.
